national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called upon Indians to dream big and lead from the front, saying that if Indian talent can lead the world’s top companies, Indian enterprises can also lead the world. Mr Modi made these remarks while addressing the gathering at the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) in New Delhi. Encouraging the ambitious spirit of the 21st-century youth, the Prime Minister celebrated their drive to build unicorns, innovate in drone technology, and create cutting-edge AI solutions. Mr Modi urged the youth to dream even bigger than previous generations, challenging them to build global consulting, accounting, financial, and legal firms that can lead the world. The Prime Minister also highlighted that the world now praises India’s policy dynamism and its status as the fastest-growing major economy. He asserted that achieving a 7.8 percent quarterly growth amid the West Asia war and global trade hurdles demonstrates India’s intrinsic capability. The Prime Minister also celebrated the success of the Make in India initiative in transforming the nation from a massive importer to a leading exporter. During his address, he shared that smartphone exports now exceed 2.5 lakh crore rupees, while domestic defense production has hit an all-time high of nearly 2 lakh crore rupees. Mr Modi also noted that the defence exports which were just 600 to 700 crore rupees in 2013-14 has reached 40 thousand crore rupees now. Mr Modi affirmed that he is not a person who walks with small and easy goals but a person who sets huge targets for the country and put his heart and soul into achieving them. Mr Modi also highlighted India’s unprecedented speed in infrastructure development and policy execution, with projects that earlier took decades now being completed in just a few years. He said rapid electrification of the railway network and a growing number of Free Trade Agreements are opening up new opportunities for the youth of the country. He cited that despite India’s first electric train running in 1925, less than 30 percent of railway lines were electrified by 2014. Highlighting his government efforts for the electrification of railway lines, Mr Modi noted that in just 12 years the central government achieved nearly hundred percent electrification.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 150 Over 500 investors, finance ministers and business leaders to attend inaugural iBRICS Summit
national_raw_news.content: More than 500 institutional investors, finance ministers and business leaders will participate in the inaugural iBRICS Summit, on the sidelines of BRICS Summit in New Delhi on 12th and 13th of this month. The two-day summit is designed to connect sovereign capital with bankable infrastructure, energy, and digital capacity projects across 21 BRICS member states and partner nations. Sovereign wealth funds, pension funds and family offices attending the iBRICS Summit manage a total wealth of 1 trillion US Dollars. They will discuss cross-border investments, non-dollar settlements and payment systems among BRICS economies. Discussions are also expected on linking national fast-payment systems such as India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and Brazil’s Pix, along with interoperability between central bank digital currencies. The summit comes at a critical juncture as BRICS economies adapt to shifting trade dynamics, US tariff pressures, and high dollar-clearing costs. The meeting is intended to connect institutional capital with infrastructure, energy and digital projects across BRICS member and partner countries. As BRICS Chair 2026, India will be hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The Summit will bring together leaders of BRICS Member and Partner Countries as well as Outreach Invitees. India’s BRICS Chairship is guided by the theme: “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, reflecting the Prime Minister’s vision of a people-centric approach rooted in the spirit of “Humanity First”.

national_raw_news.title: Nine die after drinking suspected spurious liquor in Madhya Pradesh 1 hour ago 27
national_raw_news.content: Ten people have been confirmed dead after allegedly drinking suspected spurious and illegal liquor in Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh. Sagar Collector Pratibha Pal confirmed the deaths. Around 35 people were brought to hospitals. Some of them are still in serious condition. Serious patients have been shifted to Bundelkhand Medical College and Sagar District Hospital. The case is reported from Naoroja and Ghughra Khurd villages under Banda police station area. According to the Collector, the first information was received at around 4:30 AM yesterday. Screening has now started in the affected villages. People who consumed the liquor are also being checked. The Collector said that initial findings from two to three post-mortems suggest possible consumption of methyl alcohol. Some people have been taken into custody for questioning. After the deaths, the Sagar Commissioner, IG, Collector and SP visited the affected villages and met the families of the victims. The administration has ordered some liquor shops in the area to be sealed as a precaution and their liquor samples to be collected. Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav said he has directed the minister in charge and officials to immediately investigate the matter. He said strict action will be taken and such incidents will not be tolerated by his government.
